south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: No change since the National Park Service expanded closures on September 3, 2026, confirmed unchanged today against the NPS Key Hiking Messages page last updated September 10, 2026: South Kaibab Trail is open only from the trailhead to Tip-Off Point (about 4.4 miles down) and closed below that due to hazardous conditions from flash flooding (Source: National Park Service). Ooh Aah Point (0.9 miles) and Cedar Ridge (1.5 miles), the trail's popular shorter destinations, remain within the open section. This follows the severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that destroyed nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time, and a September 8, 2026 NPS update on water system repairs did not change trail status. The NPS continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, or rockfall with little to no warning. This trail is fully sun exposed with no water source below the trailhead; confirm current water status at the trailhead before descending. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today; no active NWS alerts were found for the area today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: No change since the National Park Service expanded closures on September 3, 2026, confirmed unchanged today against the NPS Key Hiking Messages page last updated September 10, 2026: Bright Angel Trail remains open only from the trailhead to Havasupai Gardens (formerly Indian Garden) at the Tonto Trail intersection; the trail is closed below that intersection except for river-trip exchanges at Pipe Creek Beach (Source: National Park Service). This follows the severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that closed Phantom Ranch, the North Kaibab Trail, and the river-crossing bridges; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time. Stage 4 water restrictions remain in effect; most inner-canyon water sources are off, though South Kaibab Trailhead water remains on, and Grand Canyon National Park separately advises day hikers descend no farther than 1.5 miles from the upper trailhead due to elevated Inner Canyon heat risk regardless of warning status. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today; no active NWS alerts were found for the area today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, Phantom Ranch (including Bright Angel Campground, the Canteen, and cabins), and the Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings remain closed with no estimated reopening, confirmed unchanged today against the NPS Key Hiking Messages page last updated September 10, 2026 (Source: National Park Service). The closure follows the severe flash flood that struck Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, destroying nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek and damaging the Transcanyon pipeline that supplies South Rim water. A September 8, 2026 NPS update reports crews are building a temporary water intake at Bright Angel Creek and now expect water service restoration to take weeks rather than months, but this does not change trail or Phantom Ranch closure status. Phantom Ranch reservations remain cancelled and Colorado River traffic through the area remains halted. The National Park Service continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, and rockfall with little to no warning. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today; no active NWS alerts were found for the area today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
